guide.summary: Internal tool, one Workspace org (self-serve, wait none); Public app, sensitive or restricted Gmail scopes (app review); Public app, non-sensitive scopes only (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Internal tool, one Workspace org (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app, sensitive or restricted Gmail scopes (app review).

composio.note: Composio manages a Gmail OAuth app, good for prototypes. For launch, create a custom auth config with your own client ID and secret.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio provides a managed Gmail app. For production you likely need your own, so users see your brand, you get dedicated quota and can control scopes.
reasons: Users see 'Composio wants to access your account' with the managed app
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Default scopes may not include everything you need
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval

prerequisites.title: Google Cloud project
prerequisites.detail: You need a Cloud project to configure the consent screen and create the OAuth client. Billing must be enabled before publishing a Marketplace app.

prerequisites.title: Domain, home page and privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: Authorized domain ownership must be verified. The home page must be public, and the privacy policy must match your actual use of Google user data.

prerequisites.title: Demo video
prerequisites.detail: Sensitive scope verification needs a video showing how each requested scope is used.

steps.title: Choose narrowest Gmail scopes
steps.detail: List the scopes the agent needs and prefer non-sensitive ones. Draft a justification for each sensitive or restricted scope.
steps.done_when: Final scope list with written justifications exists

steps.title: Configure consent screen
steps.detail: In the Google Auth platform, set the app name, user type (Internal or External) and scopes.
steps.done_when: Branding, Audience and Data Access are saved

steps.title: Create OAuth client
steps.detail: Create a Web application OAuth client in the Google API Console. Use the redirect URI copied from the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID and secret

steps.title: Proxy the Composio callback
steps.detail: Google verifies domains, and you cannot verify Composio's callback domain. Route the callback through your own domain with a 302 redirect.
steps.done_when: Your redirect URI on your domain forwards to Composio

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the Gmail auth config through Composio's API with your client ID and secret.

steps.title: Verify domain and publish branding
steps.detail: Verify domain ownership, click Verify Branding, then Publish branding. Branding must be published before requesting data access verification.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Record the user flow that shows how each requested scope is used.

steps.title: Submit verification
steps.detail: Submit verification with justifications and the video.

steps.title: Wait for Google review
steps.detail: Sensitive scope verification typically takes 3-5 business days. Google may email for more information.

steps.title: Security assessment if required
steps.detail: If you store or transmit restricted-scope data on servers, a security assessment is required.

traps.title: Testing status expires tokens in 7 days
traps.detail: External apps in Testing have 7-day refresh tokens and a 100 test user cap, unless only basic profile scopes are used.

traps.title: Unverified apps are capped at 100 users
traps.detail: Unverified apps with sensitive or restricted scopes show warnings and are capped at 100 total users.

traps.title: Gmail refresh tokens can silently die
traps.detail: Tokens stop working after six months unused or after a password change when they carry Gmail scopes. Creating the 101st token for a client invalidates the oldest.

traps.title: Branding check expires in 7 days
traps.detail: A compliant branding result is valid for 7 days. If you do not publish in that time, you must run it again.

traps.title: No branding changes during verification
traps.detail: Branding cannot be changed while verification is in progress. You must cancel the verification first.

traps.title: Quota can throttle new users
traps.detail: A new-user authorization rate limit applies even to verified apps. Exceeding it shows users Error 403: rate_limit_exceeded.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio's name
traps.detail: The managed app shows 'Composio wants to access your account' and shares quota with other Composio users.

blockers.what_it_means: The app uses sensitive or restricted scopes without verification.
blockers.what_to_do: Submit a verification request to remove the warning.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft scope justifications and a demo video script.

blockers.what_it_means: The app is gaining new users faster than its rate limit allows.
blockers.what_to_do: Check the grant rate in the OAuth consent screen page, or request a quota increase.

blockers.symptom: Error admin_policy_enforced, or users cannot authorize
blockers.what_it_means: A customer Workspace admin has restricted or blocked the app or a service in its scopes.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer admin to set the app to Trusted or add it to their allowlist.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft an admin enablement note listing your client ID and scopes.

open_questions: How long does basic verification for non-sensitive scopes take? Check Google Cloud Console Verification Center or ask Google support.
How long does a restricted-scope security assessment take, and what does it cost? Check Google's security assessment documentation.
What is the exact rate-limit quota for a new or verified app? Check the OAuth consent screen page in the API Console.
What is the exact unverified user cap threshold? Documents say 100, but the Unverified apps page was not retrieved.
